47697-odette-s-marriage-a-novel-from-the.title: Odette S Marriage A Novel From The French Of Albert Delpit T
47697-odette-s-marriage-a-novel-from-the.creator: Unknown
47697-odette-s-marriage-a-novel-from-the.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. A strange contrast--her eyes were dark. Large, black eyes, beaming with intelligence and cultivation, but shadowed by an expression of pride and sadness. She stood before her friend, straight and slender; her lips parted in a slight smile, and the rich splendor of her hair shining in the sunbeams.

47925-pomander-walk.title: Walk*
47925-pomander-walk.creator: Unknown
47925-pomander-walk.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It lies out Chiswick way, not far from Horace Walpole's house where later Miss Pinkerton conducted her Academy for Young Ladies. It is still there, although it was actually built in 1710; but London has gradually stretched its tentacles towards it, and they will soon absorb it.

50093-keeping-up-with-william-in-which-t.title: Keeping Up With William In Which The Honorable Socrates Pott
50093-keeping-up-with-william-in-which-t.creator: Irving Bacheller
50093-keeping-up-with-william-in-which-t.description: A book by Irving Bacheller. “The other day, in the rooms of the Connecticut Historical Society, I was reading the diary of one Abigail Foote written in 1775. This, as I remember it, was an average day in her life: Mended mother's hood, set a red dye, hetchelled flax with Hannah, spun four pounds of whole wool, spun thread for harness twine, worked on a cheese basket, read a sermon of Doddridge's, scoured the pewter, milked the cows, carded wool, got supper ready, went to bed at nine.

arxiv-1805-04758.title: Search for vector-like \cmsSymbolFace ​ T \cmsSymbolFace{T} and \cmsSymbolFace ​ B \cmsSymbolFace{B} quark pairs in final states with leptons at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 \TeV
arxiv-1805-04758.description: Abstract A search is presented for pair production of heavy vector-like \cmsSymbolFace ​ T \cmsSymbolFace{T} and \cmsSymbolFace ​ B \cmsSymbolFace{B} quarks in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV . The data sample corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv , collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC in 2016.

arxiv-2009-11542.title: Practical Aspect of Privacy-Preserving Data Publishing in Process Mining Thanks: Funded under the Excellence Strategy of the Federal Government and the Länder. We also thank the Alexander von Humboldt (AvH) Stiftung for supporting our research.
arxiv-2009-11542.creator: Majid Rafiei, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
arxiv-2009-11542.description: Abstract Process mining techniques such as process discovery and conformance checking provide insights into actual processes by analyzing event data that are widely available in information systems. These data are very valuable, but often contain sensitive information, and process analysts need to balance confidentiality and utility.

arxiv-2104-08621.title: How about that Bayes: Bayesian techniques and the simple pendulum
arxiv-2104-08621.creator: Matthew Heffernan
arxiv-2104-08621.description: Abstract Physics increasingly uses Bayesian techniques for systematic data analysis and model-to-data comparison. This paper describes how these methods can be implemented to answer questions of relevance to teaching laboratories. It demonstrates the Bayesian approach to statistical modeling and model selection in a step-by-step workflow. The simple pendulum provides a demonstration with the precision commonly seen in the introductory laboratory.

arxiv-2109-13479.title: Knowledge Transfer based Evolutionary Deep Neural Network for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis
arxiv-2109-13479.creator: Arun K. Sharma, Nishchal K. Verma
arxiv-2109-13479.description: Abstract The performance of a deep neural network (DNN) for fault diagnosis is very much dependent on the network architecture. Also, the diagnostic performance is reduced if the model trained on a laboratory case machine is used on a test dataset from an industrial machine running under variable operating conditions.

arxiv-2206-14009.title: Show Me Your Face, And I’ll Tell You How You Speak
arxiv-2206-14009.creator: Christen Millerdurai, Lotfy Abdel Khaliq ∗, Timon Ulrich ∗
arxiv-2206-14009.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christen Millerdurai, Lotfy Abdel Khaliq ∗, Timon Ulrich ∗. When we speak, the prosody and content of the speech can be inferred from the movement of our lips. In this work, we explore the task of lip to speech synthesis, i.e., learning to generate speech given only the lip movements of a speaker where we focus on learning accurate lip to speech mappings for multiple speakers in unconstrained, large vocabulary settings.

arxiv-2303-04170.title: Prospects for joint cosmic ray and neutrino constraints on the evolution of trans-GZK proton sources
arxiv-2303-04170.creator: Marco Stein Muzio, Michael Unger, Stephanie Wissel
arxiv-2303-04170.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marco Stein Muzio, Michael Unger, Stephanie Wissel. We consider the prospects for future ultrahigh energy cosmic ray and neutrino observations to constrain the evolution of sources producing a proton flux above 10 10 EeV (1 EeV = 10 18 =10^{18} eV). We find that strong constraints on the source evolution can be obtained by combining measurements of the cosmic ray proton fraction above 30 30 EeV with measurement of the neutrino flux at 1 1 EeV, if neutrinos are predominantly of cosmogenic origin.

arxiv-2406-00118.title: ADEP: A Novel Approach Based on Discriminator-Enhanced Encoder-Decoder Architecture for Accurate Prediction of Adverse Effects in Polypharmacy
arxiv-2406-00118.creator: Katayoun Kobraei, Mehrdad Baradaran, Seyed Mohsen Sadeghi, Raziyeh Masumshah, Changiz Eslahchi
arxiv-2406-00118.description: Abstract Motivation: Unanticipated drug-drug interactions (DDIs) pose a significant risk of severe bodily harm, emphasizing the importance of predicting adverse effects in polypharmacy. Recent advancements in computational methods have aimed to tackle this critical challenge. Methods: This paper introduces ADEP, a novel approach that integrates a discriminator and an encoder-decoder model to address data sparsity and improve feature extraction accuracy.

arxiv-2407-01251.title: QUEEN: Query Unlearning against Model Extraction
arxiv-2407-01251.creator: Huajie Chen, Tianqing Zhu *, Lefeng Zhang, Bo Liu, Derui Wang, Wanlei Zhou, Minhui Xue
arxiv-2407-01251.description: Abstract Model extraction attacks currently pose a non-negligible threat to the security and privacy of deep learning models. By querying the model with a small dataset and using the query results as the ground-truth labels, an adversary can steal a piracy model with performance comparable to the original model.

arxiv-2410-01167.title: Measuring Solar neutrino Fluxes in Direct Detection Experiments in the Presence of Light Mediators
arxiv-2410-01167.description: Abstract The potential of the dark matter direct detection experiments to provide independent measurements on solar neutrino fluxes in the Standard Model and in the presence of the light mediators is studied in this work. We also present the sensitivity of direct detection experiments on light mediators with solar neutrinos.

arxiv-2411-04590.title: Singular stochastic delay equations driven by fractional Brownian motion: Dynamics, longtime behaviour, and pathwise stability
arxiv-2411-04590.creator: M. Ghani Varzaneh, S. Riedel
arxiv-2411-04590.description: Abstract . We study differential equations with a linear, path dependent drift and discrete delay in the diffusion term driven by a γ \gamma -Hölder rough path for γ > 1 3 \gamma>\frac{1}{3} . We prove well-posedness of these systems and establish a priori bounds for their solutions.

College of Mathematics and Statistics, Chongqing Technology and Business University,Chongqing 400067, P.R. Chinac. Department of Mathematics, Sichuan University, Che
arxiv-2412-19050.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jian-hao Kang, Zhun Gou, Nan-jing Huang a. School of Mathematics, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, Sichuan 610031, P.R. Chinab. College of Mathematics and Statistics, Chongqing Technology and Business University,Chongqing 400067, P.R. Chinac. Department of Mathematics, Sichuan University, Che. This study employs expected certainty equivalents to explore the reinsurance and investment issue pertaining to an insurer that aims to maximize the expected utility while being subject to random risk aversion.

arxiv-2501-00862.title: DiffETM: Diff usion Process Enhanced E mbedded T opic M odel Thanks: * Corresponding Author
arxiv-2501-00862.creator: 1 st Wei Shao, 2 nd Mingyang Liu, 3 rd Linqi Song*
arxiv-2501-00862.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by 1 st Wei Shao, 2 nd Mingyang Liu, 3 rd Linqi Song*. The embedded topic model (ETM) is a widely used approach that assumes the sampled document-topic distribution conforms to the logistic normal distribution for easier optimization. However, this assumption oversimplifies the real document-topic distribution, limiting the model’s performance. In response, we propose a novel method that introduces the diffusion process into the sampling process of document-topic distribution to overcome this limitation and maintain an easy optimization process.

britannica-1911-marienbad.title: Marienbad (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-marienbad.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-marienbad.description: Article 'Marienbad' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 17), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It is one of the most frequented watering-places of Europe, lying on the outskirts of the Kaiserwald at an altitude of 2093 ft., and is 40 m. Marienbad is enclosed on all sides except the south by gently sloping hills clad with fragrant pine forests, which are intersected by lovely walks.

jewish-encyclopedia-1906-gate-hebrew-ara.creator: Emil G. Hirsch

pmc-10531704.title: Murine Mast Cells That Are Deficient in IFNAR-Signaling Respond to Viral Infection by Producing a Large Amount of Inflammatory Cytokines, a Low Level of Reactive Oxygen Species, and a High Rate of Cell Death
pmc-10531704.creator: Yeganeh Mehrani, Jason P. Knapp, Julia E. Kakish, Sophie Tieu, Helia Javadi, Lily Chan, Ashley A. Stegelmeier, Christina Napoleoni, Byram W. Bridle, Khalil Karimi
pmc-10531704.description: Mat cells (MCs) are located in the skin and mucous membranes at points where the body meets the environment. When activated, MCs release inflammatory cytokines, which help the immune system to fight viruses. MCs produce, and have receptors for interferons (IFNs), which belong to a family of cytokines recognized for their antiviral properties.

pmc-11494152.title: Population monitoring and conservation implications of intra‐ and interspecific nest occupation rates in swallows
pmc-11494152.creator: José L. Tella, Cristina B. Sánchez‐Prieto, Pedro Romero‐Vidal, David Serrano, Guillermo Blanco
pmc-11494152.description: With the exception of a few groups of birds, such as large raptors and colonial seabirds, direct counts of nests cannot be conducted over very large areas for most of the abundant and widely distributed species, and thus indirect methods are used to estimate their relative abundances and population sizes.

pmc-12328261.title: Modulating Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of the Peptide Esc(1‐21) via Site‐Specific Isopeptide Bond Formation
pmc-12328261.creator: Bruno Casciaro, Daniel Ben Hur, Daniela Roversi, Carlo Vetrano, Edo Kiper, Giacomo Cappella, Federico Carneri, Eeva Tortellini, Lorenzo Stella, Neta Regev‐Rudzki, Yechiel Shai, Maria Luisa Mangoni
pmc-12328261.description: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent valid alternatives to conventional antibiotics primarily due to their mechanism of action, which consists of cytoplasmic membrane disruption. However, their clinical application is often limited by cytotoxicity at high concentrations and low intrinsic biostability. To address these limitations, various biochemical approaches have been explored.

pmc-12403472.title: The mediating effect of social networks and depressive symptoms on the relationship between older adults’ participation in volunteer activities and life satisfaction: a cross-sectional study involving Chinese older adults
pmc-12403472.creator: Yinliang Ge, Wenjun Jiang, Mo Xue, Yanxia Lyu, Lixin Hong, Kan Tian
pmc-12403472.description: BackgroundVolunteer activities have been widely acknowledged as a meaningful form of social participation for older adults, contributing to their subjective well-being. However, the psychological and interpersonal mechanisms linking volunteering to life satisfaction remain insufficiently explored. In particular, how social networks and depressive symptoms jointly mediate this relationship in the Chinese context is yet to be clarified.

pmc-12495765.title: Post-translational modifications in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: biological mechanisms and therapeutic potential
pmc-12495765.creator: Linkun Zhong, Huizheng Li, Jianhang Miao, Kuo Zhang, Ling Cui, Zhaohua Wang
pmc-12495765.description: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) remains one of the most lethal tumors, exhibiting a high recurrence rate, mortality rate and resistance to treatment. Post-translational modifications (PTMs) influence protein function by altering protein structure and play a crucial role in key signal transduction events related to tumor transformation and carcinogenesis, mainly including phosphorylation, ubiquitination, acetylation, and glycosylation.

pmc-12503875.title: Adverse Event Following Change in Brachytherapy Plaque-Cleaning Chemicals: A Case Series
pmc-12503875.creator: Jesintha Navaratnam, Thomas Bærland, Ola Nilsen, Bernt Rekstad, Rowan Faber, Nils Eide
pmc-12503875.description: IntroductionThe brachytherapy plaques used for uveal melanoma treatment are reused following sterilization processes. Here, we report patients with adverse reaction following a new cleaning procedure for brachytherapy plaques.Case PresentationsThe brachytherapy plaque sewn on the outer eyewall would be removed following the delivery of calculated radiation dose. They are reused following standard calibration testing and sterilization processes.

pmc-13196199.title: Comparison of nasolabial changes following Le Fort Ⅰ maxillary advancement versus Medpor implantation in skeletal class Ⅲ patients
pmc-13196199.creator: Xin LV, Jingyi LI, Jun CAO, Yuxin WANG, Xudong YANG, Qian ZHANG
pmc-13196199.description: ObjectiveNasolabial depression is a main aesthetic concern in patients with skeletal Class Ⅲ malocclusion, for which Le Fort Ⅰ maxillary advancement or paranasal Medpor implantation is the major treatment choice. However, the aesthetic changes following these two treatments are unclear.

pmc-13235445.title: Endovascular repair of a type IA endoleak following ALTO endograft placement using a custom-made fenestrated device
pmc-13235445.creator: Marc-Antoine Bety, Stéphane Elkouri, Laura M. Drudi, Jean-François Blair, Philippe Charbonneau
pmc-13235445.description: The ALTO endograft (Endologix, Inc) was developed to expand endovascular aneurysm repair eligibility. However, type IA endoleak remains a devastating complication associated with this device. Few reports describe management of endoleaks after ALTO implantation, and published cases are limited to open surgical explantation.

pmc-13244214.title: Small airways obstruction predicts cardiovascular disease incidence: a longitudinal study of UK Biobank
pmc-13244214.creator: Sam Bartlett-Pestell, Valentina Quintero Santofimio, James Potts, Elaine Fuertes, James P. Allinson, Jadwiga A. Wedzicha, Andre F.S. Amaral
pmc-13244214.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIsolated small airways obstruction (SAO) is common, a precursor of COPD and associated with increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. Whether isolated SAO predicts CVD incidence is unknown.MethodsUsing longitudinal data on 139 568 UK Biobank participants (median age 58 years), we calculated CVD incidence in those with, versus without, isolated SAO defined as forced expiratory volume in 3 s (FEV3)/forced expiratory volume in 6 s (FEV6) <lower limit of normal (LLN) with a normal forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1)/FEV6 ratio.

pmc-13283660.title: Predictors of Patient-Reported Outcomes in ACL Reconstruction: An Evaluation of Promis Scores after Primary and Repeat ACL Reconstruction
pmc-13283660.creator: Kevin Landrum, Sulagna Sarkar, Morgan Swanson, Brendon Mitchell, Joseph Yellin, Theodore Ganley
pmc-13283660.description: Background:Psychological factors including fear of re-injury and post-injury depression have been linked to worse outcomes following ACL reconstruction (ACLR).Hypothesis:We hypothesized that the psychological burden of repeat ACL tear negatively impacts athletes during their recovery and that patient and surgical factors may affect recovery from the first and second injury differently.

pmc-13331073.title: Pharmacovigilance Analysis of Bleeding Events Associated With Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) Using the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS)
pmc-13331073.creator: Adrian Chin Yan Chan
pmc-13331073.description: BackgroundSelective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are commonly prescribed for depressive and anxiety disorders and may increase the risk of bleeding. However, comprehensive real-world data on the patterns and distribution of SSRI-related bleeding remain limited. This study aimed to characterize bleeding adverse events associated with individual SSRIs using large-scale pharmacovigilance data.

pmc-13479083.title: Impact of IL-5 Pathway Inhibition on Circulating Eosinophil- and Remodeling-Related Biomarkers in Severe Eosinophilic Asthma
pmc-13479083.creator: Piotr Damiański, Anna Kumor-Kisielewska, Adam J Białas, Piotr Kuna, Maciej Kupczyk
pmc-13479083.description: PurposeTo assess the effects of IL-5 pathway inhibition with mepolizumab or benralizumab on circulating eosinophil-related and selected remodeling-associated biomarkers in severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA), and to determine whether these profiles differ according to four-component study-defined early clinical remission (ECR) status.Patients and MethodsThis prospective, observational, single-center cohort study included 30 adults with SEA treated with mepolizumab or benralizumab.

pmc-13573491.title: Virus-like particles in cancer immunotherapy: bridging human and veterinary medicine through one health
pmc-13573491.creator: Yingqi Zhu, Zhuangli Bi, Zichen Zhang, Miao Zhang, Qingqing Du, Mingxing Hu, Ting Zhou, Yiming Fan, Shu Zhang, Guijun Wang, Guangqing Liu
pmc-13573491.description: Virus-like particles (VLPs) are engineered nanoplatforms that mimic viral structures, offering high immunogenicity, biocompatibility, and functional versatility for cancer immunotherapy. While widely explored in human oncology as nanovaccines and targeted delivery systems for chemo-/immuno-therapeutics and genetic payloads (e.g., mRNA, siRNA, and CRISPR/Cas systems), their potential in veterinary oncology remains underexploited.
